definition: Falsifiability is the quality of a claim or research approach that keeps it open to being tested in ways that could show it to be wrong. In this context, it means designing studies so they remain scientifically testable even when methods are adjusted to better fit the experience being studied.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit or definitional description of “falsifiability” as a general property of claims/research approaches being open to being tested in ways that could show them to be wrong, so the definition’s first sentence is unsupported by the supplied source.

While the packet mentions “preserving falsifiability” in the context of reframing methodology (and discusses adjusting approaches to better match the dynamics of the OBE state), it does not state the specific meaning given in the definition’s second sentence (that falsifiability here means designing studies so they remain scientifically testable even when methods are adjusted to better fit the experience).

The packet uses “falsifiability” only in the narrow sense of preserving a study’s testability while revising methods; it does not support the broader general definition as the quality of any claim or research approach that can be shown wrong.
